B.narration:
You take out the train ticket.

“8821”

That wasn't there when you put it in your pocket. The handwriting isn't yours.

You locked the door. Somewhere, you didn't.

The air tastes of wet stone and a sudden, sharp metallic chill against your skin.

Where you are: your apartment, 6C. With you: no one. The power is out; the only light is the storm's. Something impossible has just happened, and you have gone very still.
Write ONE short sentence (under 20 words) about what you sense in the room. No names, no numbers, no quotes, no words in ALL CAPS, and don't explain anything.

D.narration:
Something small and heavy clicks against the floor by your feet. A brass key on a paper tag that says BASEMENT 07. Nobody threw it.

“STAIRWELL”

You've never seen this key before. Yet someone has written on its tag. The handwriting isn't yours.

The silence presses in, thick and heavy as damp wool.

Where you are: the roof. With you: no one. The power is out; the only light is the storm's. Something impossible has just happened, and you have gone very still.

ending.text:
You turn the lock. On the other side, a hand settles against the wood exactly where yours is.

The other night comes in quietly, the way Mara did. It smells like rain that never reached this building.

The brass key is at your feet. And it is in Mara's hand, beside you. You can feel both, like holding one thing in two hands. Your train ticket is in your hand. It always was.

Mara is in the basement. She is also beside you; you can hear her, and she can hear herself. She doesn't look surprised.

In 6D, Teo turns off his radio. "Finally," he says. To no one. Or to you.

You look at what the night left you. "8821" on the train ticket, in Mara's handwriting. "STAIRWELL" on the key's paper tag, in Mara's handwriting. Both made in a night you never lived.

The other you is standing in the doorway. They look relieved. Then uncertain. Neither of you knows who should step back.

Somewhere, you made a different choice.
